models_evaluated: U-Net spine fracture segmentation algorithm v1.0
U-Net spine fracture segmentation algorithm v2.0

links.outcome: Sensitivity and false positives of v2.0 on prospectively collected real-world WBCTs
links.effect: v2.0 sensitivities 77%-85% on Cohort 2 (n=712 WBCTs) but generated an abundance of false positives, including from trabecular structure.
links.quote: Version 2.0 also achieved decent sensitivities for Cohort 2 (sensitivities ranging between 77% and 85%) but generated an abundance of false positives.

links.outcome: Generalization of v1.0 (trained on cervical spine) to thoracic and lumbar spine fractures
links.effect: v1.0 generalized to thoracic and lumbar spine with sensitivities between 60% and 87%.
links.quote: Version 1.0 showed promising performance not only for the cervical but also the thoracic and lumbar spine due to generalization (sensitivities ranging between 60% and 87%).

screen.reason: Evaluates performance and error modes of an imaging algorithm across prospectively collected real-world cohorts, highlighting barriers to clinical deployability, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or workflow practice.
